instruction:
Use Abaqus/CAE via the Command Line Interface (CLI) or Python scripting environment to build and solve a 2D axisymmetric finite-element model of an internally pressurized thick-walled cylinder. Adopt the N-mm-MPa unit system throughout.

Geometry:
Create a 2D axisymmetric deformable solid part representing the cylinder cross-section. The radial extent is from r = 50 mm to r = 100 mm. The axial extent is from z = 0 mm to z = 10 mm.

Material:
Define a material named Steel. Set Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa and Poisson's ratio nu = 0.3. Assign this material to the entire cylinder section using a homogeneous solid section.

Mesh and Element Type:
Employ CAX4R axisymmetric solid elements. Use a structured mesh with a global seed size of 5.0 mm. Create the following node sets: ALLNODES (all nodes), INNER (r = 50 mm boundary), OUTER (r = 100 mm boundary), ZMIN (z = 0 mm boundary), and ZMAX (z = 10 mm boundary).

Boundary Conditions:
On ALLNODES, constrain axial displacement U2 = 0 to enforce the plane-strain condition. Do not apply any additional radial U1 constraint.

Loading:
Apply internal pressure p = 10 N/mm^2 on the INNER boundary (r = 50 mm), represented as equivalent axisymmetric concentrated nodal forces. For each INNER node at axial position z_i, compute the force in the positive U1 direction as:
F_i = p x 2pi x r_in x Delta z_i
where r_in = 50 mm. For the first and last INNER nodes, use half the adjacent axial interval for Delta z_i. For interior INNER nodes, use half the distance between neighboring INNER nodes for Delta z_i.

Analysis:
Create a static analysis step named Step-Pressure. Request field output for U, RF, and S. Create and submit a job named Job-Cylinder, and wait for successful completion.

Deliverables:
Save the model database to C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\Job-Cylinder.cae and the output database to C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\Job-Cylinder.odb.
